Source: MDS (SAGI), MI Social query service behind the dados.gov.br
conjunto *bolsa-familia*, yearly municipal monthly files downloaded
2026-10-06 (`_data/raw/mds/bf-YYYY.txt`, 2004-2021 and 2023-2026); municipal
quota (estimativa de famílias pobres) from the SENARC LAI response of
protocol 71003.017363/2022-16
(`_data/raw/mds/Atende_SIC_PBF_2003 a Out_2021_Acumulado_Benef.Médio.xlsx`).
Pipeline script: `_scripts/02-social-bf.R`.
Interim output: `_data/interim/bf_panel_2004_2024.rds` (2004-2019 until phase 2, step 2.2).

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(readxl)
})
options(width = 110)
```

```{r read}
bf_dir <- "_data/raw/mds"
old_files <- file.path(bf_dir, sprintf("bf-%d.txt", c(2004:2021)))
new_files <- file.path(bf_dir, sprintf("bf-%d.txt", 2023:2026))
read_old <- function(f) {
  read_csv(f, col_types = cols(ibge = col_character(), anomes = col_integer(),
                               .default = col_double()), progress = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(source_file = basename(f))
}
bf_old <- map_dfr(old_files, read_old)
bf_new <- map_dfr(new_files, ~ read_csv(.x, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                                        progress = FALSE) %>% mutate(source_file = basename(.x)))
bf_panel <- read_rds("_data/interim/bf_panel_2004_2024.rds")
munic_id <- read_xlsx("_data/raw/ibge/ibge_munic_id.xlsx", sheet = "Municípios",
                      col_types = c("text", "numeric", "text", "text"))
quota_file <- file.path(bf_dir, "Atende_SIC_PBF_2003 a Out_2021_Acumulado_Benef.Médio.xlsx")
quota_raw <- read_excel(quota_file, sheet = 1, skip = 6, col_types = "text",
                        .name_repair = "minimal")
```

## Q1. Are the yearly raw files complete and internally consistent?

What is checked: rows, municipalities, months, missingness, zeros,
negatives, positive families with zero transfers and duplicate keys per
file for 2004-2021; and the layout of the 2023-2026 files.

```{r q1-qa}
bf_old %>%
  group_by(source_file) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), municipalities = n_distinct(ibge), months = n_distinct(anomes),
            na_families = sum(is.na(qtd_familias_beneficiarias_bolsa_familia)),
            na_transfers = sum(is.na(valor_repassado_bolsa_familia)),
            zero_families = sum(qtd_familias_beneficiarias_bolsa_familia == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            zero_transfers = sum(valor_repassado_bolsa_familia == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            negative = sum(qtd_familias_beneficiarias_bolsa_familia < 0 |
                             valor_repassado_bolsa_familia < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            families_pos_transfers_zero = sum(qtd_familias_beneficiarias_bolsa_familia > 0 &
                                                valor_repassado_bolsa_familia == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            duplicate_keys = sum(duplicated(paste(ibge, anomes)))) %>%
  print(n = 20)
```

```{r q1-new}
names(read_csv(new_files[1], n_max = 0, col_types = cols(.default = col_character())))
bf_new %>% group_by(source_file) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), municipalities = n_distinct(codigo_ibge), months = n_distinct(anomes_s),
            first = min(anomes_s), last = max(anomes_s))
file.exists(file.path(bf_dir, "bf-2022.txt"))
```

**Finding.** Every file from 2004 to 2021 carries the same 5,571 six-digit
codes for twelve months, with no negative values and no duplicate keys.
Families are missing in a few dozen municipality-months per year until
2013 and in 11,152 rows of 2021 (the programme's last months before the
Auxílio Brasil substitution). In 2004-2006 the zero cells are rows where
both families and transfers are zero (930, 213 and 41 municipality-months;
in 2004, 28 municipalities for all twelve months and 55 for eight), which
is consistent with municipalities entering the programme during its
rollout rather than with reporting gaps; no row of those years has
positive families with zero transfers. That pattern appears only in 2020
(269 rows, April to December, 42 in June, the emergency-transfer months).
No file exists for 2022, and the 2023-2026 files use a new layout
(`codigo_ibge`, `anomes_s`, suffixed value columns, an average-benefit
column), with 2023 starting in March.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-05-b: panel truncated at 2019; the 2020-2026
evidence feeds task 1.2, settled at Q6 (phase 2, step 2.2, D-2026-10-22-a).
**Assertion.** `02-social-bf.R`, raw-state block (files present, columns,
twelve months per year, no duplicates, no negatives).

## Q2. Which month represents the year?

Candidates: February, June, July, September, November. Criteria, as in the
lost script: stability relative to the previous month, distance from the
yearly median, completeness, for beneficiary families and for the transfer
per family, 2004-2019.

```{r q2-decision}
candidate_months <- c(2, 6, 7, 9, 11)
bf_m <- bf_old %>%
  filter(anomes >= 200401, anomes <= 201912) %>%
  mutate(year = anomes %/% 100L, month = anomes %% 100L,
         families = qtd_familias_beneficiarias_bolsa_familia,
         per_family = if_else(families > 0, valor_repassado_bolsa_familia / families, NA_real_))
stability <- bf_m %>%
  group_by(ibge, year) %>% arrange(month, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(fam_lag = lag(families), val_lag = lag(per_family), lag_month = lag(month)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(month %in% candidate_months, lag_month == month - 1) %>%
  transmute(month, fam_instability = abs(families - fam_lag) / fam_lag,
            val_instability = abs(per_family - val_lag) / val_lag) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(fam_instability_p50 = median(fam_instability, na.rm = TRUE),
            fam_jump_20 = mean(fam_instability > 0.2, na.rm = TRUE),
            val_instability_p50 = median(val_instability, na.rm = TRUE),
            val_jump_20 = mean(val_instability > 0.2, na.rm = TRUE))
centrality <- bf_m %>%
  group_by(ibge, year) %>%
  mutate(fam_med = median(families, na.rm = TRUE), val_med = median(per_family, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(month %in% candidate_months) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(fam_distance = mean(abs(families - fam_med) / fam_med, na.rm = TRUE),
            val_distance = mean(abs(per_family - val_med) / val_med, na.rm = TRUE))
completeness <- bf_m %>%
  filter(month %in% candidate_months) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(na_fam = mean(is.na(families)), zero_fam = mean(families == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            na_val = mean(is.na(per_family)))
stability %>% left_join(centrality, by = "month") %>% left_join(completeness, by = "month")
```

**Finding.** On the re-acquired files June is the most central month
(smallest mean distance to the yearly medians of families and of the
transfer per family, 1.9 and 1.4 percent) with completeness equal to the
other candidates, while February is the most stable month relative to
the previous one (lowest median change and lowest share of jumps above
20 percent); September and November return an infinite distance because
some municipality-years have a zero median. The inherited pair (June as
reference, February as alternative) is kept; the author may revisit the
ranking, since the lost script's prose credited June with the lowest
instability as well.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-05-a: `BF_REF_MONTH = 6`, `BF_ALT_MONTH = 2`.
**Assertion.** `02-social-bf.R`, output block (both months present for
every municipality-year).

## Q3. Is the implied transfer per family plausible across years?

```{r q3-per-family}
bf_m %>%
  filter(month == 6) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(p1 = quantile(per_family, .01, na.rm = TRUE), p50 = median(per_family, na.rm = TRUE),
            p99 = quantile(per_family, .99, na.rm = TRUE), max = max(per_family, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  print(n = 16)
bf_panel %>%
  filter(bf_ref_month == 6) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(families_millions = sum(bf_families_n, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6,
            transfers_bn_brl_2024 = sum(bf_transfers_total_brl_2024, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e9,
            per_family_brl_2024 = transfers_bn_brl_2024 * 1e9 / (families_millions * 1e6)) %>%
  print(n = 16)
```

**Finding.** The nominal transfer per family dips in 2005-2007 and then
rises with each benefit revision; the real series (2024 BRL) shows the
coverage expansion to 2014 and the stabilisation afterwards, the known
trajectory of the programme; the tails stay within a few multiples of the
median.
**Decision.** none required.
**Assertion.** none (distributional).

## Q4. Do the municipal quota values look plausible?

What is checked: the LAI workbook's layout, the period-to-year mapping,
the quota ratio distribution in 2006-2007, the fourteen Mato Grosso cases
of task 1.4, and the zero-family rows of task 1.8.

```{r q4-workbook}
names(quota_raw)[1:9]
quota_munic <- quota_raw %>%
  select(UF, MUNICÍPIOS, IBGE, starts_with("ESTIMATIVA")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(IBGE), str_detect(IBGE, "^[0-9]{7}$")) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("ESTIMATIVA"), as.numeric))
nrow(quota_munic)
quota_munic %>% filter(IBGE == "1100015")
bf_panel %>% filter(geocode == "1100015", bf_ref_month == 6) %>% select(year, bf_quota) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = bf_quota)
```

```{r q4-outliers}
mt_cases <- c("Alta Floresta", "Apiacás", "Barra do Bugres", "Confresa", "Guarantã do Norte",
              "Juara", "Nova Canaã do Norte", "Nova Olímpia", "Pontes e Lacerda",
              "São José dos Quatro Marcos", "Santa Carmem", "Salto do Céu",
              "São Félix do Araguaia", "Nova Monte Verde")
ratio_0607 <- bf_panel %>%
  filter(bf_ref_month == 6, year %in% 2006:2007) %>%
  left_join(munic_id %>% select(geocode = munic_id, munic, uf), by = "geocode")
ratio_0607 %>%
  summarise(p50 = median(bf_families_quota_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
            p99 = quantile(bf_families_quota_ratio, .99, na.rm = TRUE),
            above_3 = sum(bf_families_quota_ratio > 3, na.rm = TRUE),
            above_3_mt = sum(bf_families_quota_ratio > 3 & uf == "MT", na.rm = TRUE))
ratio_0607 %>%
  filter(uf == "MT", munic %in% mt_cases) %>%
  group_by(geocode, munic) %>%
  summarise(families = max(bf_families_n), quota_2006_08 = first(bf_quota),
            ratio = max(bf_families_quota_ratio), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(ratio))
ratio_0607 %>% filter(bf_families_quota_ratio > 3, !(uf == "MT" & munic %in% mt_cases)) %>%
  select(geocode, munic, uf, year, bf_families_n, bf_quota, bf_families_quota_ratio)
```

```{r q4-zero}
bf_panel %>% filter(bf_ref_month == 6, bf_families_n == 0) %>%
  left_join(munic_id %>% select(geocode = munic_id, munic, uf), by = "geocode") %>%
  count(year)
```

**Finding.** The workbook (header on row 7) carries one row per
municipality with a 7-digit code and four estimates of poor families, one
per period; the pipeline assigns them to 2004-2005, 2006-2008, 2009-2011
and 2012-2019, which is the constant-within-period pattern of the lost
`bf-quotas.xlsx`. The 2006-2007 ratio has a median near one (1.04) and a
99th percentile of 2.1. Sixty-nine municipality-years exceed 3, 61 of
them in Mato Grosso; the fourteen municipalities of task 1.4 are the
largest cases (3.1 to 12.5) and other Mato Grosso municipalities (Barra
do Garças among them) and a few in Mato Grosso do Sul and Paraná also
exceed 3. The values exceed 3 in the source itself: the LAI workbook is
the quota's origin, so the outliers are source-borne, not a tidy-step
error, and the fix (if any) needs an external quota series. Rows with
zero beneficiary families against a positive quota exist nationally in
June 2004 (98), 2005 (23) and 2006 (4).
**Decision.** D-2026-10-07-g (period mapping); task 1.4 stays open as a
source question; task 1.8 (zero rows) open. Task 1.4 settled at Q4b (phase 2,
step 2.1, D-2026-10-21-a).
**Assertion.** `02-social-bf.R`, raw-state and output blocks (header
names, 5,570 unique codes, every panel row of a listed municipality has a
quota).

## Q4b. Why do the Mato Grosso quotas fail, and does realignment repair them? (phase 2, step 2.1, 2026-10-21)

What is checked: the stored estimate against the workbook's own
December families, state by state; the row order of the Mato Grosso
block; the offset between each Mato Grosso row and its alphabetical
position; the realigned estimates for the task 1.4 municipalities and
Cuiabá; where the zero "até 2005" estimates land; and the pipeline output
after the fix.

```{r q4b-states}
est_cols <- names(quota_raw)[str_detect(names(quota_raw), "ESTIMATIVA")]
# quota_raw keeps the workbook's blank header cells as "" names, which
# dplyr verbs refuse, so the columns are pulled by position and name.
wb <- tibble(sheet_row = seq_len(nrow(quota_raw)) + 7L,
             IBGE = quota_raw$IBGE, UF = quota_raw$UF, munic = quota_raw$MUNICÍPIOS,
             q_ate05 = as.numeric(quota_raw[[est_cols[1]]]),
             q_0608  = as.numeric(quota_raw[[est_cols[2]]]),
             q_0911  = as.numeric(quota_raw[[est_cols[3]]]),
             q_12    = as.numeric(quota_raw[[est_cols[4]]]),
             fam_dec2006 = as.numeric(quota_raw[[21]]),   # "2006", Famílias (Dezembro)
             fam_dec2010 = as.numeric(quota_raw[[37]])) %>%
  filter(!is.na(IBGE), str_detect(IBGE, "^[0-9]{7}$"))
wb %>%
  group_by(UF) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            cor_0608 = round(cor(fam_dec2006, q_0608, use = "complete.obs"), 2),
            med_ratio = round(median(fam_dec2006 / q_0608, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
            n_above_3 = sum(fam_dec2006 / q_0608 > 3, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_below_0.2 = sum(fam_dec2006 / q_0608 < 0.2, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(cor_0608) %>%
  print(n = 6)
```

```{r q4b-rows}
mt <- wb %>% filter(UF == "MT")
bind_rows(head(mt, 3), tail(mt, 2)) %>% select(sheet_row, IBGE, munic, q_0608, fam_dec2006)
mt_alpha <- order(mt$munic, method = "radix")
mt <- mt %>% mutate(alpha_pos = match(row_number(), mt_alpha),
                    shift = alpha_pos - row_number())
table(mt$shift)
mt %>% filter(shift > 0) %>% select(sheet_row, munic, alpha_pos, shift)
```

```{r q4b-realign}
realigned <- mt %>% select(sheet_row, IBGE, munic, shift, fam_dec2006, fam_dec2010)
for (v in c("q_ate05", "q_0608", "q_0911", "q_12")) {
  realigned[[v]] <- NA_real_
  realigned[[v]][mt_alpha] <- mt[[v]]
}
realigned <- realigned %>%
  mutate(r06_stored = round(fam_dec2006 / mt$q_0608, 2),
         r06_realigned = round(fam_dec2006 / q_0608, 2),
         r10_realigned = round(fam_dec2010 / q_0911, 2))
cases_14 <- c("5100250", "5100805", "5101704", "5103353", "5104104", "5105101",
              "5106216", "5106232", "5106752", "5107107", "5107248", "5107750",
              "5107859", "5108956")
realigned %>%
  filter(IBGE %in% c(cases_14, "5103403")) %>%
  select(munic, shift, q_ate05, q_0608, q_0911, q_12, fam_dec2006,
         r06_stored, r06_realigned, r10_realigned) %>%
  arrange(desc(r06_stored)) %>%
  print(n = 15)
abslog <- function(r) median(abs(log(r[is.finite(log(r))])))
tibble(block = c("MT as stored", "MT realigned", "other 26 states as stored"),
       cor_0608 = c(cor(mt$fam_dec2006, mt$q_0608),
                    cor(realigned$fam_dec2006, realigned$q_0608),
                    with(wb %>% filter(UF != "MT"), cor(fam_dec2006, q_0608, use = "complete.obs"))),
       med_abs_log_ratio = c(abslog(mt$fam_dec2006 / mt$q_0608),
                             abslog(realigned$fam_dec2006 / realigned$q_0608),
                             abslog(with(wb %>% filter(UF != "MT"), fam_dec2006 / q_0608))),
       p95_ratio = c(quantile(mt$fam_dec2006 / mt$q_0608, .95),
                     quantile(realigned$fam_dec2006 / realigned$q_0608, .95),
                     quantile(with(wb %>% filter(UF != "MT"), fam_dec2006 / q_0608), .95, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
realigned %>% filter(r06_realigned > 2.5 | r06_realigned < 0.3 | r10_realigned > 2.5 | r10_realigned < 0.3) %>%
  select(munic, q_ate05, q_0608, q_0911, fam_dec2006, fam_dec2010, r06_realigned, r10_realigned)
```

```{r q4b-zero}
# Zero "até 2005" estimates: stored on Guiratinga and Indiavaí, realigned
# onto the municipalities installed after 2005.
mt %>% filter(q_ate05 == 0) %>% select(munic, q_ate05, q_0608)
realigned %>% filter(q_ate05 == 0) %>% select(munic, q_ate05, q_0608, q_0911)
```

```{r q4b-output}
# Pipeline output after the fix (bf_panel read at setup).
mt_out <- bf_panel %>%
  filter(geocode %in% mt$IBGE, bf_ref_month == 6, year %in% 2006:2007)
summary(mt_out$bf_families_quota_ratio)
bf_panel %>%
  filter(bf_ref_month == 6, year %in% 2006:2007, bf_families_quota_ratio > 3) %>%
  left_join(munic_id %>% select(geocode = munic_id, munic, uf), by = "geocode") %>%
  count(uf)
```

**Finding.** The stored estimate tracks the workbook's own December
families in every state but Mato Grosso (correlation 0.97 or above against
0.12). The Mato Grosso block lists Santa Cruz do Xingu and União do Sul on
its first two rows and the other 139 municipalities alphabetically, while
the four estimate columns run in strict alphabetical order over all 141
rows: each estimate sits two rows above its municipality up to Santa Cruz do
Xingu's alphabetical slot (113 municipalities), one row above up to União
do Sul's slot (21), and in place for the last five. Cuiabá's row holds 376
poor families for 2006-2008 and Conquista D'Oeste's row holds Cuiabá's
16,882; the workbook's own coverage column carries the same misalignment
(Cuiabá at 5,393 percent in 2006), so the error is in the LAI response as
delivered, not in the download or the tidy step. Realigned by name, the
Mato Grosso block has the correlation (0.994) and the ratio distribution
(median absolute log ratio 0.14, 95th percentile 1.3) of the other states,
all fourteen task 1.4 municipalities fall to ratios between 0.6 and 1.2,
and the two zero "até 2005" estimates land on Ipiranga do Norte and
Itanhangá, two of the nine municipalities created after the 2000 census
(task 1.6). The only residual outlier is
Itanhangá's 2006 ratio of 0.14, a rollout-year value of a new municipality.
The three Mato Grosso do Sul and one Paraná municipalities above 3 are
consistent with their states' pattern and stay as stored. After the fix no
Mato Grosso municipality exceeds 3 in 2006-2007.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-21-a (supersedes D-2026-10-05-n): the four period
columns of the Mato Grosso rows are realigned in `02-social-bf.R`; the
raw file is untouched.
**Assertion.** `02-social-bf.R`, realignment block (141 Mato Grosso rows,
the two displaced geocodes first, the rest in alphabetical order, shift
counts 113/21/5) and output block (June 2006 families-quota correlation
above 0.95 in Mato Grosso, no 2006 ratio at or above 3).

## Q5. Do the six-digit MDS codes map to the IBGE geocodes, and how do Mojuí dos Campos and Santarém appear?

```{r q5-codes}
geocode_map <- munic_id %>% transmute(ibge = str_sub(munic_id, 1, 6), geocode = munic_id)
tibble(lookup_rows = nrow(munic_id), unique_prefixes = n_distinct(geocode_map$ibge),
       mds_codes = n_distinct(bf_old$ibge), matched = sum(unique(bf_old$ibge) %in% geocode_map$ibge))
bf_old %>%
  filter(ibge %in% c("150475", "150680"), anomes %% 100 == 6, anomes %/% 100 %in% 2011:2016) %>%
  select(ibge, anomes, qtd_familias_beneficiarias_bolsa_familia) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = ibge, values_from = qtd_familias_beneficiarias_bolsa_familia)
```

**Finding.** The seventh IBGE digit is a check digit, so the six-digit
prefix identifies every one of the 5,571 municipalities of the lookup, and
every MDS code matches one. Mojuí dos Campos carries its own beneficiary
counts from 2014 only; Santarém's earlier counts are not split, as
inherited.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-07-h.
**Assertion.** `02-social-bf.R`, raw-state block (unique prefixes, every
MDS code matched) and output block (no NA geocode).

## Q6. What do the 2020-2026 files hold, and how is the series extended to 2024? (phase 2, step 2.2, 2026-10-22)

What is checked: the monthly transfer per beneficiary family and the
family count on the 502 biome municipalities from 2019 to 2026, across
the Auxílio Emergencial rounds, the Auxílio Brasil gap and the re-created
programme; the LAI workbook's annual totals for 2019-2021 on the same
municipalities as a second accounting of the same years; the new layout's
code coverage, parsing and average-benefit column; and the pipeline
output after the extension, by regime and reference month.

```{r q6-monthly}
biome <- unique(read_rds("_data/reference/panel_amz_2000_2020_final_phase1.rds")$geocode)
biome6 <- str_sub(biome, 1, 6)
bf_new_num <- bf_new %>%
  transmute(ibge = codigo_ibge, anomes = as.integer(anomes_s),
            qtd_familias_beneficiarias_bolsa_familia = as.numeric(qtd_familias_beneficiarias_bolsa_familia_s),
            valor_repassado_bolsa_familia = as.numeric(valor_repassado_bolsa_familia_s),
            avg_benefit = as.numeric(pbf_vlr_medio_benef_f), source_file)
monthly <- bind_rows(bf_old %>% filter(anomes >= 201901), bf_new_num %>% select(-avg_benefit)) %>%
  filter(ibge %in% biome6) %>%
  group_by(anomes) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), families = sum(qtd_familias_beneficiarias_bolsa_familia, na.rm = TRUE),
            transfers_nominal = sum(valor_repassado_bolsa_familia, na.rm = TRUE),
            per_family_nominal = transfers_nominal / families,
            na_rows = sum(is.na(qtd_familias_beneficiarias_bolsa_familia)),
            families_pos_transfers_zero = sum(qtd_familias_beneficiarias_bolsa_familia > 0 &
                                                valor_repassado_bolsa_familia == 0, na.rm = TRUE))
monthly %>% filter(anomes <= 202412) %>% print(n = 60)
monthly %>% mutate(year = anomes %/% 100L) %>% group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(months = n(), families_min = min(families), families_max = max(families),
            per_family_min = min(per_family_nominal, na.rm = TRUE),
            per_family_max = max(per_family_nominal, na.rm = TRUE))
```

```{r q6-workbook}
# Yearly blocks of the LAI workbook: four columns per year (families in
# December, total R$, coverage, average benefit); 2018 starts at column 69,
# 2019 at 73; 2021 reports January-October.
wb_years <- tibble(year = 2019:2021, first_col = c(73L, 77L, 81L)) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(rows = list(quota_raw[quota_raw$IBGE %in% biome, ]),
         families_dec = sum(as.numeric(rows[[first_col]]), na.rm = TRUE),
         total_brl_nominal = sum(as.numeric(rows[[first_col + 1L]]), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% select(-rows, -first_col)
monthly_year <- monthly %>% mutate(year = anomes %/% 100L) %>%
  filter(year %in% 2019:2021) %>% group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(monthly_file_total_nominal = sum(transfers_nominal))
wb_years %>% left_join(monthly_year, by = "year") %>%
  mutate(ratio_file_to_workbook = monthly_file_total_nominal / total_brl_nominal)
```

```{r q6-layout}
old_codes <- unique(bf_old$ibge); new_codes <- unique(bf_new_num$ibge)
missing_code <- setdiff(old_codes, unique(bf_new_num$ibge[bf_new_num$anomes < 202511]))
tibble(old_codes = length(old_codes), new_codes = length(new_codes),
       missing_before_nov_2025 = paste(missing_code, collapse = ","),
       name = munic_id$munic[str_sub(munic_id$munic_id, 1, 6) %in% missing_code],
       parse_na_families = sum(is.na(bf_new_num$qtd_familias_beneficiarias_bolsa_familia)),
       parse_na_transfers = sum(is.na(bf_new_num$valor_repassado_bolsa_familia)),
       duplicate_keys = sum(duplicated(paste(bf_new_num$ibge, bf_new_num$anomes))))
bf_new_num %>%
  mutate(implied = valor_repassado_bolsa_familia / qtd_familias_beneficiarias_bolsa_familia,
         gap = avg_benefit - implied) %>%
  summarise(rows = n(), within_1_brl = mean(abs(gap) < 1, na.rm = TRUE),
            gap_p99 = quantile(abs(gap), 0.99, na.rm = TRUE), gap_max = max(abs(gap), na.rm = TRUE))
```

```{r q6-output}
# Pipeline output after the extension (bf_panel read at setup).
bf_panel %>% distinct(year, bf_ref_month, bf_regime) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = bf_ref_month, values_from = bf_regime, names_prefix = "month_") %>%
  filter(year >= 2019)
bf_panel %>%
  filter(geocode %in% biome, year >= 2019) %>%
  group_by(bf_ref_month, year, bf_regime) %>%
  summarise(n_families = sum(!is.na(bf_families_n)), families = sum(bf_families_n, na.rm = TRUE),
            per_family_brl_2024 = sum(bf_transfers_total_brl_2024, na.rm = TRUE) / families,
            n_quota = sum(!is.na(bf_quota)), quota_ratio_median = median(bf_families_quota_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_pea_ratio = sum(!is.na(bf_transfers_pea_brl_2024)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(bf_ref_month, year)
```

**Finding.** The 2020 and 2021 files have the 2004-2019 layout and
coverage; the 2023-2026 files have a new layout that parses without loss
and covers 5,570 codes until October 2025, the missing one being Boa
Esperança do Norte (MT, installed 2025, outside the sample); its
average-benefit column is the ratio of the two stored columns rounded by
the provider and is not carried. On the biome municipalities the
beneficiary count is stable from 2019 to October 2021 (2.11 to 2.24
million) while the transfer per family in the monthly files falls from
about R$ 212 in January-March 2020 to R$ 6-7 in April-August and
R$ 35-41 in September-December, returns to R$ 206-210 in January-March
2021, halves to R$ 99-106 in April-October 2021 and is empty from
November 2021 to February 2023 (no file for 2022, 2023 starting in
March). These are the two Auxílio Emergencial rounds: families paid the
emergency aid were taken off the Bolsa Família payroll, so the monthly
service reports the residual disbursement. The LAI workbook, which
accounts for the entitlement, shows no fall on the same municipalities
(R$ 5.58 bn in 2020 against 5.54 bn in 2019, 4.60 bn for January-October
2021); the monthly files sum to the workbook's total exactly in 2019, to
a third of it in 2020 and to two thirds in January-October 2021. June, the
reference month, lies inside the substitution window in both years;
February does not. From March 2023 the re-created programme pays about
R$ 660-700 per family nominal (2.6-2.8 times 2019 in 2024 BRL) to 41 percent
more biome families, with no quota series (the workbook ends in October
2021) and no PEA denominator after 2022. After the extension the interim
grid runs 2004-2024 for both months: 2004-2019 values unchanged, 2020-2021
as reported under `pbf_emergency_aid` (June) and `pbf` (February), 2022
and February 2023 empty under `auxilio_brasil`, 2023-2024 under
`pbf_2023` with the quota and PEA ratios NA.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-22-a (series to 2024 across both layouts, 2022
empty; supersedes D-2026-10-05-b, closes D-2026-10-05-q), D-2026-10-22-b
(substitution months stored as reported, `bf_regime` added and carried
into the panel), D-2026-10-22-c (quota through 2021, NA after).
**Assertion.** `02-social-bf.R`, raw-state block (both layouts' columns,
no 2022 file, 5,571 and 5,570 codes with the one missing code named, the
new layout parsed without NA, deflator through 2024) and output block
(grid size, regime sequence by month and year, Auxílio Brasil rows empty,
June transfer per family below half of 2019's in the substitution years
and below a tenth in 2020, above twice 2019's under the 2023 programme,
quota NA after 2021).

## Q7. Are the zero-beneficiary rows true zeros? (phase 2, step 2.7, 2026-10-28)

What is checked: the rows of the 2004-2024 grid with zero families, by
month and year; the sample's June rows with a zero quota ratio, with
February of the same year and June of the next; and the rows with
positive families and zero transfers (task 1.8; D-2026-10-28-c).

```{r q7-zeros}
names_tbl <- read_rds("_data/interim/mapbiomas_deforestation_amz_1987_2023.rds") %>%
  distinct(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation)
bf_panel %>% filter(bf_families_n == 0) %>% count(bf_ref_month, year)
bf_panel %>% filter(bf_families_n == 0, bf_transfers_total_brl_2024 > 0) %>% nrow()
bf_panel %>% filter(bf_families_n > 0, bf_transfers_total_brl_2024 == 0) %>% count(bf_ref_month, year)
june <- bf_panel %>% filter(bf_ref_month == 6)
june %>%
  filter(geocode %in% names_tbl$geocode, bf_families_n == 0) %>%
  select(geocode, year, bf_quota, ratio = bf_families_quota_ratio) %>%
  left_join(bf_panel %>% filter(bf_ref_month == 2) %>% select(geocode, year, feb_families = bf_families_n),
            by = c("geocode", "year")) %>%
  left_join(june %>% transmute(geocode, year = year - 1L, next_june_families = bf_families_n),
            by = c("geocode", "year")) %>%
  left_join(names_tbl, by = "geocode") %>%
  select(municipality, state_abbreviation, year, bf_quota, ratio, feb_families, next_june_families) %>%
  arrange(year, municipality)
```

**Finding.** Zero-family rows exist only in 2004 (98 in June, 100 in
February), 2005 (23, 32) and 2006 (4, 4), always with zero transfers,
and never afterwards. In the sample the fourteen June rows are ten 2004
municipalities that are zero in February too and paid in June 2005, and
Ipiranga do Norte and Itanhangá, installed in 2005, in 2005 (quota 0,
ratio NA) and 2006 (quota 93 and 100, ratio 0), paid from 2007. This is
the programme's rollout, so a zero of the payment file is a true zero and
the quota ratio is 0, not NA. Positive families with zero transfers occur
only in June 2020 (42 rows), the emergency-aid substitution months of
D-2026-10-22-b. No value changes.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-28-c.
**Assertion.** `02-social-bf.R`, output block (zero families only in
`BF_ROLLOUT_YEARS` and then with zero transfers; positive families with
zero transfers only in `BF_ZERO_TRANSFER_YEARS`).
